clue.text: Married one — so plucky if suffering from this

definitions.text: Married one — so plucky if suffering from this

parts.words: Married one — so plucky if suffering from this
parts.note: a person who dreads wedlock yet walks down the aisle anyway would have to be brave indeed

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who wed despite a crippling fear.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a hatred or dread of wedlock, which would make getting wed an act of courage.

clue.text: Not still in the race, old boy!

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the mile is a classic running race

explanation.surface: An old pal still running in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Something able to move is the opposite of motionless.

clue.text: (Hence Dutch) courage

parts.note: courage is the plain sense; Dutch courage is bravery from drink, hence the alcohol sense

explanation.surface: A remark on boldness found in a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means mettle or pluck, and also strong liquor, the source of Dutch courage.

clue.text: Tourists look to them for a change

definitions.text: Tourists look to them for a change

parts.words: Tourists look to them for a change
parts.note: change suggests novelty, but refers to the ceremony of the changing of the guard that visitors watch

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers seeking variety.
explanation.walkthrough: The Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace is a London tourist sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers of the Household regiments perform the ceremony of relieving the palace guard.

clue.text: Deed Maud held to be all confused

definitions.text: Deed Maud held to be all confused

indicators.note: all confused says the letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Maud's opinion of some act is that it was utterly muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thoroughly bewildered and unable to think clearly fits this compound adjective.

clue.text: Doctor superior to cattleman

parts.note: over means above or superior to

explanation.surface: A physician outranks a rancher.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman who drives livestock to market is called by this name.

clue.text: Trump, say, with such a diamond

indicators.note: say signals a word as it is spoken

parts.note: to ruff is to trump in card games

explanation.surface: A remark about Trump and a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: A rough diamond is an uncut stone, or a person of good character but coarse manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncut gems are described as unpolished, as in the phrase for a good but unrefined person.

clue.text: Corruption of archdeacon and laity perhaps

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Graft among church officials and parishioners.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open to bribery is a form of corruption.

clue.text: Very hot day — many going in the car

indicators.note: going in means one piece enters the other

parts.note: a roaster is a scorching day
D is the Roman numeral for 500, so many

explanation.surface: A sweltering day with crowds piling into the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An open two-seater sports car is a type of automobile.

clue.text: Trick admitted by gangs of freebooters

indicators.note: something admitted by a group is let inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: bands are gangs of people
to rig is to fix or trick

explanation.surface: A scam welcomed by groups of pirates.
explanation.definitionFit: Freebooters and bandits are both lawless plunderers.

clue.text: Sheridan's Spanish governess

parts.note: Sheridan wrote a comic opera named after a Spanish chaperone of young ladies

explanation.surface: A character from Sheridan: a chaperone in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Brinsley Sheridan's 1775 comic opera takes its title from the older woman who guards a young Spanish lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish term is for an older woman acting as chaperone and governess to girls.

clue.text: Male superintendent ? Only by oral report

definitions.text: Male superintendent ? Only by oral report

parts.words: Male superintendent ? Only by oral report
parts.note: said out loud male sounds like mail, and the woman in charge of a post office oversees the mail

explanation.surface: A rumour that some boss is a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman in charge of a post office manages the post, a mail superintendent.

clue.text: One landed in Scotland

parts.note: landed reads like arriving by air or sea, but means owning land, as a Scottish estate owner does

explanation.surface: A traveller touching down north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots title is given to a landed proprietor owning an estate.

clue.text: Through which we may narrowly escape, with net losses here?

definitions.text: Through which we may narrowly escape, with net losses here?

parts.words: Through which we may narrowly escape, with net losses here?
parts.note: gaps in a fishing net let fish slip away, and gaps in rules let people slip out of obligations

explanation.surface: Fish wriggling free through gaps in a torn net.
explanation.definitionFit: Small gaps or openings, literally in a net or figuratively in a law, allow escape.

clue.text: The time a harp composition shook the Colosseum

indicators.note: a composition puts the letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A harp piece played so loudly it rocked the Roman arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shook' is only a link here; 'composition' rearranges THE TIME A HARP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum is the most famous example of an oval Roman arena for spectacles.

clue.text: Just unusually quiet and capable

indicators.note: unusually says the letters come in an uncommon order

parts.note: able means capable

explanation.surface: Fair-minded, oddly reserved and competent.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and impartial treatment is just.

clue.text: Equestrian gear of an Indian city

definitions.text: Equestrian gear of an Indian city

parts.words: Equestrian gear of an Indian city
parts.note: riding breeches are named after the Rajasthan city where they originated

explanation.surface: Riding kit from a city in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding trousers tight below the knee take their name from a city in Rajasthan.

clue.text: Rolling in the aisles in such pain ?

definitions.text: Rolling in the aisles in such pain ?

parts.words: Rolling in the aisles in such pain ?
parts.note: helpless laughter is being in this state, and sharp side pains bear the same name

explanation.surface: An audience laughing so hard it hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in this state means laughing uncontrollably, and the word also names sharp pains in the side.

clue.text: Showing off various oriental outstations

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take a different arrangement

parts.note: oriental means eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: Flaunting a variety of far-eastern outposts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious, flashy behaviour designed to attract notice is showing off.

clue.text: The root of chassis corrosion

parts.note: a chassis is the frame of a car, standing for the vehicle
rot is decay or corrosion

explanation.surface: The underlying cause of rust on a vehicle frame.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange vegetable is a root crop.

clue.text: But this city is also in Missouri

definitions.text: But this city is also in Missouri

parts.words: But this city is also in Missouri
parts.note: the city named after this Midwestern state lies partly across the border in Missouri

explanation.surface: A geography point about a city in Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: Kansas City straddles the border, with its larger half in Missouri.
explanation.definitionFit: The state shares its name with a city mostly located in neighbouring Missouri.

clue.text: A display of arms rather than the result of brood

definitions.text: A display of arms rather than the result of brood

parts.words: A display of arms rather than the result of brood
parts.note: the word looks like the noun for what a brood produces by hatching, but is really a heraldic panel

explanation.surface: Not chicks from a clutch but a coat of arms on show.
explanation.walkthrough: A hatchment is a diamond-shaped board bearing the arms of a dead person, hung on their house.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic term names a funeral panel bearing a coat of arms.

clue.text: Language spoken in the Cochin district

indicators.note: in signals letters lying within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tongue used around Cochin.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Indian tongue is a language.

clue.text: Triple crown one found in Ireland's hill

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: Tara is the famous hill of the High Kings in Ireland
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A three-tiered headpiece discovered on an Irish hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal crown with three tiers is called a triple crown.

clue.text: Universal refusal to name an island

parts.note: U is the film rating for universal viewing
shan't is a blunt refusal

explanation.surface: Everyone declines to give an island's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Ushant is a French island off Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: This rocky isle off the tip of Brittany marks the entrance to the Channel.

clue.text: " Melancholy Of — and blackest Midnight born " (Milton)

definitions.text: " Melancholy Of — and blackest Midnight born " (Milton)

parts.words: " Melancholy Of — and blackest Midnight born " (Milton)
parts.note: the opening of L'Allegro names Melancholy's parent as the three-headed hound of Hades

explanation.surface: A quotation from Milton about Melancholy's dark parentage.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's L'Allegro begins 'Hence, loathed Melancholy, Of Cerberus and blackest Midnight born'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the mythical dog guarding the underworld gates.

clue.text: Songster is discovered in swindle

indicators.note: discovered in says one piece is found inside another

parts.note: to skin someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A singer found to be part of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: This small finch is a songbird, a songster in crossword terms.

clue.text: Boss's tea brew may suit firemen

indicators.note: a brew is a mixture, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: all letters of the word with its apostrophe s are used

explanation.surface: The chief's cuppa might be fit for the fire brigade.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireproof mineral was once made into protective suits for firefighters.
